founder_questions.q: Who may resume a batch stranded at 'applying' or 'undoing', and when? Today the same person can resume it at any moment. A resume that arrives while the first apply is still running (a reload during a long menu import) races it: the optimistic revision check stops any double write, but it can leave a row mislabeled and return a 409 to the first request.
options: Same person, any time (current)
Same person, but only after the batch has sat untouched for N minutes (a lease), so a request still in progress is never treated as a crash
Any manager or owner on the house, with the same lease
Time-boxed auto-resolve: a job marks stranded rows 'unconfirmed' and closes the batch
founder_questions.recommendation: Same person with a short lease (for example 5 minutes on updated_at). It keeps the small permission surface Codex built and closes the reload race. Widen it to any manager only if a departed person's stuck batch turns out to be a real case.
founder_questions.why: The previous code had no recovery path at all. Recovery authority and its timing are a genuine design fork, and the any-time resume that shipped cannot tell a crash from a request still in progress.

founder_questions.q: Are notification_preferences per person, or per person per house? Migration 20260813090000 left this open and OD-95/OD-98 reference it. Arrival's undo now keys on the row's own id, which is safe under either answer. But arrival's read of the row (arrival.service.ts:341-346, keyed on user_id with maybeSingle) fails outright for a person who has one row in each of two houses.
options: Leave it open. Arrival's undo is safe either way, and a person with two rows gets an error, never data loss
Decide now (per person per house), and have arrival and NotificationsService key on (restaurant_id, user_id)
founder_questions.recommendation: Leave it open for this train. Decide it with the notifications work that owns NotificationsService's upsert and push subscriptions.
founder_questions.why: It predates this lane. Arrival no longer loses data under either answer, but the notifications page stays broken for people with rows in two houses until it is decided.

Why: ADR 0149 row 16 and the founder's round-4 answer require /authorize to reach the full-purpose bar. The gateway serves and seals the disclosure. Each grant keeps a receipt holding the seal id and a digest of the words shown. Each return page reads the outcome back. What:
- Gateway integrations: a provider grant now needs a consent seal (seal kind 'integration_grant') and writes an integration_consent_receipts row. The provider callback parks an encrypted code and redirects to /authorize/complete#state&request&delivery. The delivery secret is created only at that moment. To complete, a request must hold both the tab's own proof and that delivery secret. A wrong value in either voids the state. This closes account injection through a forwarded provider URL (KL audit D1). A second callback voids the state too (J1). An origin-allowlist failure never returns 500. Membership is re-checked through the new currentRestaurantRole helper, which fails closed (503 when unreadable, refused when revoked).
- Gateway ask-readings: a catalogue of 15 readings with a runner, sources, a folio store and bound replies. Sonnet picks at most 8 measured cells, and every caption is built from measured labels. BoundAskController exposes it. POST /ask/folios returns 503 until ASK_LAUNCHED is set.
